name: Oso Grande

profile.address: 725, 6th Street Northwest, Old Town, Albuquerque, Bernalillo County, New Mexico, 87102
profile.reading:
Oso Grande is a colocation and internet infrastructure facility in the Old Town area of Albuquerque, New Mexico, at 725 Sixth Street Northwest. The company traces its roots to 1984, when it was founded as New Mexico Technet, one of the earliest regional internet service providers in the American Southwest and a participant in the early buildout of academic and commercial networking in New Mexico. It later rebranded as Oso Grande, and today operates as a locally based colocation and connectivity provider serving businesses, schools and government agencies across the state, an unusually long operating history for a facility of its size and a rarity among the mostly hyperscale and multinational operators elsewhere in this registry.

The company's own published materials describe the facility as SOC 2 compliant, indicating an independently audited set of controls around security, availability and confidentiality of hosted systems and data. Oso Grande also states that its backup generation is sized to roughly 125 percent of the facility's load, giving it headroom beyond a straight one to one backup ratio, paired with more than 30 hours of on site fuel reserve. That combination points to a facility built for extended utility outages rather than brief ride through events, which matters in a region where wildfire smoke, extreme heat and occasional grid stress can extend outages beyond what a few hours of diesel would cover.

Oso Grande does not publish its total IT capacity in megawatts, its raised floor or white space square footage, or a public tenant list, which is typical for a regional colocation operator that markets primarily to local enterprise and public sector customers rather than hyperscale cloud tenants. The Old Town Albuquerque address places the facility in one of the city's oldest commercial districts, blocks from the historic plaza, suggesting an adaptive use of an existing building rather than a purpose built greenfield data hall, consistent with the company's long, incrementally grown history rather than a recent large scale construction project. No public building permit, expansion filing or capacity upgrade specific to this address has been identified. As with many independent regional providers, additional detail would most likely come directly from Oso Grande through a sales inquiry rather than through public filings.

reading:
Oso Grande Technologies is a small, locally owned colocation and connectivity provider in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and its history is considerably older and more interesting than its size suggests. By the company's own account the organisation began in 1979 as New Mexico TechNet, created at the instigation of a former state governor and Senator Pete Domenici to develop communications and provide public access to information in a state whose economy already turned on the hard sciences work at Los Alamos and Sandia national laboratories. That account names the founders in the company's own words and is repeated here without independent confirmation of the individuals involved. By the mid 1980s TechNet was managing the state's fibre optic network and internetworking with DARPA before the word internet was in general use, which puts it among the earliest regional network operators in the American Southwest. A for profit arm, TechNet For Profit, was spun out in 1993. Data centre and internet services began in 2000, and an employee led rebranding in 2001 produced the Oso Grande name. A founding year of 1984 appears on the facility level record for this operator and does not match the company's own 1979 date, and the discrepancy is noted rather than resolved.

Today the company sells colocation, disaster recovery, remote hands, web hosting, internet access, carrier cross connects and fibre networking, aimed at businesses, schools and government agencies within New Mexico rather than at hyperscale tenants. Its published address is 725 Sixth Street Northwest, unit C, Albuquerque 87102, on the edge of the Old Town and downtown area. It names Randal Kohutek as chief executive and Dennis Jontz as chairman, and lists a SOC 2 Type I attestation and Better Business Bureau accreditation. Earlier company material described standby generation sized to roughly 125 percent of facility load with more than 30 hours of on site fuel, a design aimed at riding through extended utility outages rather than brief interruptions. That is a standby generation figure and says nothing about IT load.

What is not established is most of what a capacity database would want. There is no published IT load in megawatts, no utility service size, no on site generation, no white space or raised floor square footage, no cabinet count and no public carrier list. An earlier version of this entry carried an approximate 1 megawatt figure drawn from a third party directory listing. No operator statement, filing, permit or utility docket supports that number, and it has been removed rather than repeated, because a directory estimate presented as capacity is exactly the kind of figure that propagates through registries unchallenged.

The registry row itself is a single OpenStreetMap node rather than a mapped building footprint, so it marks a point on Sixth Street Northwest rather than a structure, and the unit designator carried in its tags points to suite level occupancy within a larger building rather than a standalone data centre shell. That is a normal arrangement for a small carrier hotel style operation in a downtown core, where the attraction is the fibre already in the street and in the building rather than land or power headroom, but the building's ownership, age and size are not established on the public record.
